Our publications sit at the intersection of infectious disease dynamics, outbreak forecasting, public health decision-making, and the practical business of making models behave when data are incomplete. A full and continuously updated list is available on [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=qZ0DYksAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao).

## Selected Papers

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature}
### Improving Outbreak Forecasts Through Model Augmentation
This PNAS paper introduces epimodulation, a way to improve empirical outbreak forecasts by adding epidemiological dynamics after forecasts are generated. It tackles a very practical forecasting problem: models often get weird right when epidemics get interesting.

[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2508575122) · [Blog post](blog/2025-11-12-epimodulation/)
:::

::: {.feature}
### Optimizing Disease Outbreak Forecast Ensembles
This Emerging Infectious Diseases paper asks a practical question for forecast hubs: how many models are needed to build a strong ensemble? The answer helps clarify participation targets, baseline comparisons, and design principles for collaborative forecasting systems.

[Paper](https://doi.org/10.3201/eid3009.240026) · [Blog post](blog/2024-10-28-ensemble-size/)
:::

::: {.feature}
### Annual Hospitalizations For COVID-19, Influenza, And RSV
This work compares the burden of three major respiratory viruses in the United States during 2023-2024. It connects infectious disease modeling to the healthcare planning questions that motivate much of the lab's forecasting work.

[Paper](https://doi.org/10.3201/eid3103.240594)
:::

::: {.feature}
### FluSight Forecast Evaluation
This collaborative evaluation of FluSight forecasts helped define and assess a new target for laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations, a key step for improving operational respiratory virus forecasting.

[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50601-9)
:::
:::

## Earlier Publications

Earlier work includes studies on COVID-19 scenario modeling, testing strategies, surveillance, intervention effectiveness, arboviral emergence, mpox reproduction number, and collaborative influenza forecasting. Use the [Google Scholar profile](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=qZ0DYksAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao) for the complete indexed list.
